    "issue_type": "Missing error handling for JSON parsing",
    "severity": "high",
    "file": "t54.js",
    "line": 10,
    "evidence": "res.on(\"end\", () => resolve(JSON.parse(body)));",
    "llm_reasoning": "The code assumes that the response body will always be valid JSON. If the server returns an error page (HTML) or an empty response, JSON.parse will throw an unhandled exception, causing the promise to remain pending or crash the process. This makes the function fragile and difficult to debug for consumers.",
    "suggested_fix": "Wrap JSON.parse in a try-catch block: res.on('end', () => { try { resolve(JSON.parse(body)); } catch (e) { reject(e); } });",

    "suggested_fix": "Check the status code inside the callback: if (res.statusCode < 200 || res.statusCode >= 300) { reject(new Error('Request failed with status ' + res.statusCode)); }",
